question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
response: I read the common guide first, then package query --help to learn the CLI shape and the explicit --take bound. I requested package query --explain to identify dependency facets and saw that depends starts-with matches direct dependencies while dependency-target selects a framework group. My first -Q lookup used the facet name and failed, so I read its error and requested -Q Packages for the precise --where syntax. I then ran one Microsoft.Extensions.* query with --take 40, a Polly dependency prefix, and net10.0 scope. Its JSON gave the matching package, inspected version, selected .NETStandard2.0 group, and direct Polly declarations; stderr stated that the candidate limit was reached. Those facts answered the requested package, dependency classification, framework evidence, and family-exhaustiveness questions. A separate package inspection would only repeat manifest details already returned, while transitive traversal would address a broader search that this 40-candidate result could not exhaust, so I stopped.
